provider.notes: Registered at gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1763-1766; dispatched at gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:436-437 (which also accepts 'ifly'). MODEL KEY: iFlytek has no model parameter. Rows are keyed by the vendor's business.domain value, which matches how the gateway picks the socket today: a model string containing 'realtime', 'stream' or 'ist' selects the real-time socket and anything else, including an empty string, selects the short-form socket with domain 'iat' (gateway/src/core/stt/iflytek/config.rs:422-436). default_model is therefore 'iat' although the vendor has no model field. Three glob rows, '*realtime*', '*stream*' and '*ist*', mirror that substring routing so that a string the gateway sends to the real-time socket is not described as the short-form product; they are marked assumed and should be deleted when model routing becomes an exact lookup. The client targets the international (Singapore) hosts only. NO FILE UPLOAD: segmentation by file upload is neither needed nor possible. Every product that can serve a call is a WebSocket stream, and the only file API is an asynchronous job with a stated floor of about 20 seconds. STREAMING CLIENT (adapter native, known_broken; read from code and vendor documentation, never run against the vendor; paths under gateway/src/core/stt/iflytek/ unless stated): (1) A short-form session holds one utterance: the vendor's final result sets session_ended (client.rs:253-257), the next tick returns Completed (client.rs:191-195) and the supervisor exits without redialling (gateway/src/core/websocket/reconnectable_stream.rs:374-376). Every later send_audio fails (client.rs:841-844) while is_ready stays true (client.rs:827-829). The repository test states this is by design (gateway/tests/mock_endpoint_e2e.rs:578-580). (2) Results are slices the client is expected to join and, for 'rpl' slices, replace; the client emits each slice alone (messages.rs:481-486, client.rs:489-508), so a final carries only the last fragment, and an empty last slice emits no final at all. (3) Confidence is the average of a field the vendor documents as reserved, or an invented 0.95 (messages.rs:489-500). (4) On the short-form socket the end of an utterance is the vendor's silence timeout vad_eos, 2000 ms by default (config.rs:439), so end of speech to final is at least two seconds. (5) On the real-time socket the client always sends domain 'iat' (config.rs:436) and vad_eos, where the vendor documents the domains ist_open, ist, ist_hy, ist_huanyu and sp_ist_vais, the parameter 'punc', 16 kHz audio only and no vad_eos; and it marks a result final only when data.status is 2, which on that socket follows the client's own end marker, so probably no final arrives before hang-up (inferred). (6) An unknown language falls back to Mandarin (config.rs:416), and Cantonese is sent as language 'zh_hk' with accent 'cantonese' (config.rs:126, :174), which is not a vendor value: the vendor selects Cantonese with language 'zh_cn' plus accent 'cantonese' on both sockets. (7) vad_eos is copied from the customer's endpointing_ms without a bound (config.rs:469-471; validate() at config.rs:496-525 never checks it), although the vendor's maximum is 10000 ms. (8) Once the first frame has gone, the loop sends a frame every 40 ms even when it has no audio (client.rs:198), so zero-length frames flow during silence, the vendor's 10 second idle timer never fires, and silence is never withheld. (9) After the first utterance the session is not closed or redialled: each audio frame the caller sends produces one error message to the client (gateway/src/handlers/ws/audio_handler.rs:130-133; LiveKit path gateway/src/handlers/ws/config_handler.rs:2947-2954). PER-UTTERANCE SOCKET (adapter planned_commit, which no release builds): open a short-form session when the gateway's detector reports speech (pre-roll first), stream in real time, send the end marker {"data":{"status":2}} when the detector reports end of speech, then open the next session; rotate before 60 seconds. Set vad_eos to its maximum of 10000 ms so the vendor's silence timeout does not end the session first. The vendor asks for 1280 bytes every 40 ms and warns that a shorter interval may cause incorrect recognition. Results must be assembled by slice number with replacements applied. This adapter shares its speech start and stop events with the segmented engine. STATE TODAY: the streaming client is the native transport, enabled from Release 0, groundwork and honest refusal, and reported as known broken in ready.stt rather than refused (integration decisions, section 15); each native transport carries its defect. No release builds a file or commit transport for iFlytek (decisions section 12: its only file interface is a slow asynchronous job). Speed Transcription task types, which today's client silently streams as domain 'iat', are refused from Release 3, default on. config/pricing.rs has no iFlytek entries, so rows carry no pricing_key.

segment_profile.rationale: The audit's profile for per-utterance sessions. No silence is appended because under real-time pacing it delays the final by its own length; the end marker is sent at end of speech instead. 55 seconds because the vendor closes a session at 60. One in flight because sessions are sequential. 5000 ms from end marker to final is a proposal; no latency is published.
